item.title: Tangle Invariants Valued in Derived Categories of Sheaves and the Rouquier Complex
item.description: arXiv:2611.07046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop effective calculation tools for constructing categorified invariants of tangles and knots, following the work of Cautis and Kamnitzer. These invariants, originally constructed by means of Fourier-Mukai transform functors between derived categories of coherent sheaves on certain iterated flag varieties, can be given an alternative algebraic description by using tilting bundles. We use this method and provide several examples of its application, in the hope of showing its utility to explicit pen-and-paper computations. This tilting-bundle method also allows us to lift the construction from derived to homotopy categories of complexes of modules, reducing the calculation of tangle invariants to a type of categorified matrix algebra, where the matrices in question have maps between their elements and calculations get turbocharged with chain homotopy.
item.dc:creator: Jian Qiu, Alex Takeda

item.title: The odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(3,7)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a class of interesting algebraic varieties --- odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(k,2n+1)$ and study them with an emphasis on the case of the submaximal odd biisotropic symplectic Grassmannians $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(n,2n+1)$, which we call catalecticant varieties. The main result of the paper is a construction of a full exceptional collection in the derived category of the catalecticant sixfold $\operatorname{S_2Gr}(3,7)$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Kuznetsov

item.title: Isospectral Deformations of Diagonal Matrices by Symmetric Matrices in Dimension Four
item.description: arXiv:2611.07150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a diagonal matrix $D$ with distinct diagonal entries in an algebraically closed field $K$ we study the symmetric matrices $Q$ with entries in $K$ such that the affine line $D+tQ$ has the same eigenvalues in $K$ as $D$. We study the equality of characteristic polynomials, $\chi_{D+tQ}(x)=\chi_D(x) \text{ for all }\: t\in K$ and examine the resulting system of equations. For generic diagonal matrices of size at most $4$ we show that only the trivial symmetric matrix $Q=0$ satisfies this isospectral condition. We use this result to compute the degree of a field extension that appears in the invariant theory of quadratic forms under congruence action.
item.dc:creator: Hari Asokan

item.title: Values of differentials of plane branches: block decomposition and semiroots
item.description: arXiv:2611.07255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the passage of special gaps from a Zariski semiroot to a plane branch. A decomposition into rectangular blocks allows us to compute the maximal valuations of the coefficients of differentials and describe the image of the transition map. We treat vertical and horizontal decompositions, as well as decompositions with alternations, obtaining criteria for the preservation of special gaps. For towers whose ramification indices after the first are all equal to two, the value semigroup of the branch and the special gaps of the first semiroot determine the special gaps of the branch.
item.dc:creator: Marcelo Osnar Rodrigues de Abreu

item.title: Brauer groups of generalised Markoff surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.07454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero with $a,b,c\in k^\times$ and let $m\in k\setminus\{0,4abc\}$. We compute the Brauer group of the generalised Markoff surface $ax^2+by^2+cz^2-xyz=m$. We also construct several counterexamples to the integral Hasse principle, which are explained by the Brauer--Manin obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Zheshuai Tian, Dasheng Wei

item.title: The Chow ring of a wonderful compactification
item.description: arXiv:2611.07507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The theory of wonderful compactifications provides a common framework encompassing the constructions of important varieties such as the Fulton-MacPherson configuration spaces, the moduli space of $n$-pointed stable rational curves, and the De Concini-Procesi models of subspace arrangements, and, more generally, of smooth compactifications in which the subvarieties in a building set are replaced by a simple normal crossings boundary divisor. We give a presentation of the Chow ring of a wonderful compactification, assuming only that the Chow ring of the ambient variety surjects onto that of each subvariety in the induced arrangement. Our results recover and extend many previously known presentations and apply to a broad range of new examples.
item.dc:creator: Patricio Gallardo, Javier Gonz\'alez-Anaya, Jos\'e Luis Gonz\'alez

item.title: Bernstein-Sato polynomials of generic Pfaffian ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.07571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine all roots and their multiplicities in the Bernstein--Sato polynomial of every generic Pfaffian ideal. In the nonmaximal case, the roots lie in explicit rational windows indexed by the rank strata. Integral roots retain their label multiplicities, whereas every nonintegral root is simple, including values with several labels. The proof combines graph-module relations, skew Capelli operators, central characters, and a weighted Mellin integral. We deduce the strong motivic monodromy conjecture for Pfaffian ideals, with pole orders bounded by Bernstein--Sato root multiplicities. For Pfaffians of size $2r$, the largest possible root multiplicity as the matrix size varies is $\lfloor(\sqrt{8r+1}-1)/2\rfloor$. In the nonmaximal case we also prove that the nonunipotent part of the Verdier specialization has zero nilpotent monodromy. Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, Pfaffian ideal, root multiplicities, strong monodromy conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Chen Huaiqing Zuo

item.title: Fermat quotients with CM Jacobians and trivial automorphism group
item.description: arXiv:2611.08176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F_n$ be the Fermat curve of degree $n$ over $\mathbb Q$, and let $D_n=F_n/S_3$ be its quotient by coordinate permutations. We prove that $D_n$ has trivial geometric automorphism group for every $n\ge 11$ with $\gcd(n,6)=1$. Its Jacobian has complex multiplication. For $n=11$, this Jacobian is absolutely simple of dimension five. We construct an isogeny over $\mathbb Q$ of degree $11^5$ from $\operatorname{Jac}(D_{11})$ to the Jacobian of $y^{11}=x(1-x)^2$. For primes $p\equiv 1\pmod 3$, we also consider the metacyclic quotients $C_p$ of $F_p$ over $\mathbb Q$. By a theorem of Carocca, Lange and Rodr\'iguez, their Jacobians are absolutely simple and have complex multiplication. We prove that $C_p$ has trivial geometric automorphism group if and only if $p\ge 19$. Write $p=r^2+rs+s^2$ with $r,s$ positive integers. The natural degree-three cover $Y_p\to C_p$ satisfies $\operatorname{gon}(Y_p)=r+s$, so $\operatorname{gon}(C_p)\ge \lceil(r+s)/3\rceil$. Since $g(C_p)=(p-1)/6$, both the genus and the gonality of $C_p$ tend to infinity with $p$.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Tafazolian

item.title: Torsion points in families of elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.08190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the specialization of torsion points in one-parameter degenerations of elliptic curves with singular fibers of Kodaira type. We describe the resulting torsion curves, their ramifications, intersection multiplicities, and irreducible and connected components.
item.dc:creator: Ester Sgallov\'a

item.title: Butler's conjecture for K3 curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.08333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Butler's conjectures predict that, on a general smooth curve $C$ of genus $g\ge3$, a general coherent system $[\mathcal{O}_C\otimes V\xrightarrow{\varphi}E]$ with semistable underlying bundle $E$ and $\dim V>\operatorname{rk}(E)$ has surjective evaluation map $\varphi$ and stable kernel. In this paper, we prove Butler's conjectures for $g\ge8$ in the two cases in which the Brill-Noether geometry of a general curve is known, namely rank one and the range $\mu(E)>2g-2$. By deformation and openness, it suffices to establish the result on a single Brill-Noether-Petri general curve. We do so for curves on K3 surfaces of Picard rank one, using the wall-crossing theory of coherent systems developed by the first two authors.
item.dc:creator: Soheyla Feyzbakhsh, Aliaksandra Novik, Angela Ortega

item.title: Kappa Classes on the KSBA Space of Stable Toric Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2611.08337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study kappa classes on the normalization of the main component of the Koll\'ar--Shepherd-Barron--Alexeev(KSBA) moduli space of stable toric pairs. Using a toric model obtained by a lattice modification, we compute all kappa classes on the moduli space by giving a combinatorial formula for their intersection numbers with all torus-invariant cycles. In particular, we identify the first normalized kappa class with the GKZ polarization of the toric variety corresponding to the secondary polytope. For interval configurations, we also obtain a closed formula for all top intersection products of normalized kappa classes.
item.dc:creator: Byeol Han

item.title: Ramification of Weighted Central Paths and Super-linear Interior-Point Methods for Semi-definite Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.07080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The local convergence of primal-dual interior-point methods for semi-definite optimization is closely tied to the regularity of the central path at its limiting point. Without strict complementarity, the central path can exhibit fractional power asymptotics and need not be differentiable in the ordinary barrier parameter. We show that this obstruction can be removed simultaneously for a family of weighted \AHO~central paths. More precisely, there exists a common ramification exponent $N$ such that all weighted paths in a fixed neighborhood of the identity become analytic at the limiting point after the reparametrization $\mu\mapsto\mu^N$. Using higher-order derivatives of these reparametrized paths, we construct a feasible $p$th-order predictor-corrector interior-point method. Under a uniform predictor regularity condition, and without assuming strict complementarity, we prove that the normalized complementarity gaps converge with $Q$-order at least $(p+1)/\rho$, where $\rho$ is the reparametrization exponent used by the method. We also establish super-linear convergence of the simultaneously vanishing primal-dual blocks, derive an explicit quantitative reduction bound throughout the predictor regularity region, and obtain a doubly logarithmic outer iteration bound once the iterates enter the local super-linear regime. Finally, we illustrate the predicted higher-order behavior on a collection of degenerate and non-degenerate semi-definite optimization problems.
item.dc:creator: Ali Mohammad-Nezhad, Pouya Sampourmahani, Tamas Terlaky

item.title: Local Homological Mirror Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.07202v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local mirror symmetry, originated from the work of Chiang-Klemm-Yau-Zaslow arXiv:9903053, indicated a potential relation between mirrors to a vector bundle and mirrors to its zero section. In this paper, we constructed a homological mirror to these local varieties and proved the corresponding Homological Mirror Symmetry statement. As an application, we constructed infinite families of exotic Weinstein sectors as mirrors to Hirzebruch surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Si-Yang Liu, Kyungmin Rho

item.title: On the Topology of the Set of Nonnegative Forms That Are Not Sums of Squares
item.description: arXiv:2611.07252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the topology of the normalized space of real nonnegative forms of degree $2d$ in $n$ variables that are not sums of squares. Whenever it is nonempty, we prove that it is path-connected but not acyclic, and in particular not contractible. We give explicit bounds on the degrees in which its reduced homology can be nonzero. In the two minimal nonempty cases, we show an embedding of an exterior algebra into the cohomology ring, and prove containment of the binary octahedral and binary icosahedral groups, respectively, in its fundamental group.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian Illmer, Tim Netzer

item.title: On explicit units in a family of cubic fields and the arithmetic of curves arising from powers of these units
item.description: arXiv:2611.07333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For an integer $b\neq0,1$ let $K_b$ be the cubic field generated by the unique real root of $x^3-3bx-b^3$, let $\eta_0$ be its fundamental unit, and let $\eta_b$ be the explicit unit studied in the companion paper (arXiv:2609.37389). Write $\eta_b=\eta_0^{n(b)}$. Deciding whether $n(b)$ is divisible by $q$ amounts to finding the integral points of a plane curve $C_q$ of degree $2q$. We prove that for every integer $q\ge1$ the curve $C_q$ is irreducible with $g(C_q)=\binom{q-1}{2}$, the genus of a smooth plane curve of degree $q$ rather than of degree $2q$. The proof is not a genus computation but a structural one: $C_q$ is the inverse image, under the $q$-power map of a two-dimensional torus, of the curve traced by the minimal polynomial of $\eta_b$ as $b$ varies, and the formula falls out of two applications of Riemann-Hurwitz in the resulting tower. As a consequence the problem splits into exactly three regimes: $q=2$ rational, $q=3$ elliptic, and $q\ge4$ of general type. In particular only finitely many $b$ have $q\mid n(b)$ for each $q\ge4$. A lower bound for linear forms in two logarithms gives $n(b)<6082138$ for every $b$, so $n(b)\in\{1,2\}$ for all but finitely many $b$, though not effectively. We add two computations: $n(b)$ is determined outright for $|b|\le10^{30}$, and the rational points of $C_4$ are determined by quadratic Chabauty, giving $4\mid n(b)\iff b\in\{-75,-3,5,96\}$. We state precisely which parts of the latter rest on certified arithmetic and which do not. Finally, we show that $K_b\cong K_{b'}$ with $b\neq b'$ holds for $\{b,b'\}=\{-1,5\}$, and otherwise only if one of the two parameters, $c$ say, satisfies $|c|>10^{30}$ and $n(c)$ is divisible by a prime $q\ge5$. There are only finitely many such pairs.
item.dc:creator: Iwao Kimura, Hikaru Umemoto

item.title: Two-row Schur times Schubert via parallel classes of positroid varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.07351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Schubert structure constants are intersection numbers of Schubert varieties. Finding positive combinatorial formulas for these constants remains a major open problem. We resolve this problem when one of the indexing permutations corresponds to a two-row partition. Our approach uses increasing chains, introduced by Sottile for the one-row case, and builds on the skew Schubert functions studied by Bergeron and Sottile. The key step is to connect increasing chains and these functions with the parallel classes of positroid varieties.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Yu

item.title: Functors from Lagrangian correspondences for wrapped sheaf categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.07466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the category of sheaves on a manifold with microsupport in a singular conic Lagrangian, and more generally microsheaves on the Lagrangian skeleton of a Weinstein manifold with stop, which are equivalent to ind-completions of partially wrapped Fukaya categories. Compact objects in these categories are obtained as wrappings of constructible sheaves with perfect stalks; they correspond to objects built from exact Lagrangians in finitely many steps. We give a microlocal criterion on constructible (micro)sheaves with perfect (micro)stalks which guarantees that the corresponding wrapped sheaves induce integral kernels that preserve compact objects of these categories. This generalizes a result of Gao on Lagrangian correspondences between fully wrapped Fukaya categories.
item.dc:creator: Sheel Ganatra, Christopher Kuo, Wenyuan Li, Haosen Wu

item.title: The residual map as a stratified fibration over the resonance arrangement
item.description: arXiv:2611.07499v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a stratum $\mathcal{H}(\mu)$ of meromorphic one-forms on a Riemann surface with prescribed orders of zeros and poles, the residual map assigns to each differential the collection of its residues at the poles. In this paper, we prove that the residual map is a locally trivial topological fibration over each open flat of the stratification induced by the resonance arrangement. To give an algebro-geometric proof of this result, we introduce a refined compactification of the projectivized stratum $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{H}(\mu)$, namely the moduli space of residue-aligned multi-scale differentials $\operatorname{RAMS}(\mu)$. We prove that the projectivized residual map extends to $\operatorname{RAMS}(\mu)$ as a stratified fibration over the projectivized resonance arrangement, thereby yielding a resolution of the projectivized residual map. This approach naturally extends to the analogue of the residual map for strata of $k$-differentials. Complementing the algebro-geometric approach, we also develop a flat-geometric point of view. In genus zero, each isoresidual fiber carries a canonical higher-dimensional analogue of a translation structure. These fibers admit a metric completion whose boundary has a modular interpretation in terms of the WYSIWYG compactification, for which we provide explicit local models. Isoresidual fibers admit a polyhedral cell decomposition whose geometry varies linearly with the underlying configuration of residues in period coordinates. Degenerations of these cells occur precisely when resonance conditions are satisfied, providing a geometric proof that the residual map is a stratified fibration. Finally, certain isoresidual fibers admit natural interpretations as Hurwitz spaces of branched covers, yielding unexpected homeomorphisms between moduli spaces of covers with prescribed ramification profiles.
item.dc:creator: Dawei Chen, Scott Mullane, Nick Salter, Guillaume Tahar

item.title: Arithmetic Kac Theory for Ramified Species
item.description: arXiv:2611.07549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K=k((t))$, where $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, and let $\Lambda$ be an acyclic ramified species over $K$. An indecomposable $\Lambda$-module can split after extending $K$. The number of its distinct geometric indecomposable summands is the degree of its residue endomorphism field $\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)/\operatorname{rad}\operatorname{End}_\Lambda(M)$. We use the positive roots and cyclic automorphism of the unfolded quiver to determine the number of isomorphism classes at every nonzero rank and residue degree $e\ge1$: it is zero, an explicitly computable finite number, or $|K|$. For every invariant imaginary root of the unfolding, including at nonprimitive ranks, we construct a smooth invariant family of absolutely indecomposable representations whose rational quotient by the change-of-bases group has dimension $1-q_d(\beta)$. We characterize ranks admitting absolutely Schur representations by the Schur roots of the unfolded quiver. For the associated species over finite fields, we realize the polynomials counting absolutely indecomposable representations as graded traces of the unfolding automorphism on preprojective BPS cohomology. Galois-orbit formulas and M\"obius inversion then recover the counts at each residue degree. Finally, we prove an all-rank symmetrizable analogue of Kac's constant-term conjecture: the constant term of the polynomial counting all indecomposables, rather than only absolutely indecomposable ones, equals the corresponding Kac--Moody root multiplicity. This constant is independent of the symmetrizer and modulation.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
item.description: arXiv:2611.07849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a genus-two hypergeometric family whose Jacobians have real multiplication by $\Q(\sqrt5)$. We identify the relevant primitive factor and integral rank-two monodromy; at one real embedding the projective image is $\Delta(2,5,\infty)$, while the conjugate image is nondiscrete. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ Borel covers are quadratic pullbacks of genus-one triangular modular curves. The same rank-two systems have finite-field hypergeometric Frobenius traces, yielding the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation twisted by the character of $2$.
item.dc:creator: Devendra Tiwari

item.title: Tilting bundles and modifying modules in relative dimension one
item.description: arXiv:2611.07987v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For projective morphisms $\pi:Y\to X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ over noetherian complete local rings, with fibres of dimension at most one and $\mathbf{R}\pi_*\mathcal{O}_Y\cong\mathcal{O}_X$, we construct a tilting fan from cones of pretilting bundles. Maximal cones parametrize tilting bundles, and facet adjacency encodes irreducible mutation. Completeness in positive rank is equivalent to finiteness of tilting bundles modulo line-bundle twists. For closed fibres that are split ADE highest-root cycles or their Stein contractions, we identify tilting bundles with chambers of restricted affine Tits cones and determine the fan. Over normal Gorenstein complete local domains, reflexive pushforward takes pretilting bundles on normal projective birational models with fibres of dimension at most one and $\pi^!\mathcal{O}_X\cong\mathcal{O}_Y$ to modifying modules. Pushforwards of canonical tilting bundles recover models as module blowups and detect contractions by additive containment, yielding an Auslander--McKay embedding. The hypersurfaces $R=S[[u,v]]/(uv-f)$, with $S$ a regular complete local ring and $f\in S$ a nonzero nonunit, generalize type $A$ Du Val surfaces and $cA_n$ threefolds to arbitrary dimension. We classify modifying modules by divisor flags and rank-one reflexive twists; flag blowups turn the embedding into an equivalence. If $f$ has $r\ge2$ prime factors counted with multiplicity, reflexive pushforward on any maximal-flag model gives a mutation-preserving surjection from tilting bundles, parametrized by chambers of affine type $\widetilde{A}_{r-1}$, to maximal modifying modules. Its fibres are affine Weyl group orbits determined by repeated factors. All maximal-flag models and maximal modification algebras are derived equivalent. These algebras are noncommutative crepant resolutions exactly when $S/(p)$ is regular for every prime factor $p$ of $f$.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga

item.title: Universal $x$-$y$ duality in equivariant topological recursion and quartic Kontsevich model
item.description: arXiv:2611.08018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Topological recursion is a universal procedure that generates an infinite family of multi-differentials with different interpretations in various areas of mathematics. Recently, a new understanding of topological recursion has emerged from $x$-$y$ duality, which relates two such families through explicit formulae. We study $x$-$y$ duality, its parametrised version, and symplectic duality in the setting of equivariant topological recursion. We explicitly analyse the pole structure of the resulting dual families and provide recursive formulae for the different types of polar parts. In contrast to classical topological recursion, the dual family has additional poles at fixed points of the group action, and at anti-diagonals determined by the group action. We show that the partition function $Z_P(E)=\int_{H_N} e^{-N\,\mathrm{Tr}(E\Phi^2+P(\Phi))}d\Phi$ of the Kontsevich matrix model with arbitrary potential $P$, where $d\Phi$ is the Lebesgue measure on Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices and $E$ a positive matrix, admits a Fock space realisation related to the character expansion of the IZHC integral. The Fock space framework provides two mutually $X$-$Y$ dual families of multi-differentials relative to an implicitly defined spectral curve $(X,Y)$. The solution $Y(X)$ succeeds for the quartic Kontsevich model with potential $P(\Phi)=\frac{\lambda}{4}\Phi^4$. We identify a network of duality transformations and symplectic shifts which relate the quartic Kontsevich model with the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant spectral curve. The proposed construction yields a conjectural all-genus solution to the quartic Kontsevich model, which reproduces recursive structures previously established for genus $g\leq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hock, Jakob Lindner, Raimar Wulkenhaar

item.title: Uniform Three-Fold Product Expansion of Algebraic-Geometry Codes over a Fixed Field
item.description: arXiv:2611.08172v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A collection of classical codes $C_1,\dots,C_m$ has product expansion if every low-weight word in the sum of their extensions to the product space can be written as a sum of words supported on few lines, each line being a codeword of the corresponding $C_i$. For $m=2$ product expansion is equivalent to robust testability of the tensor code, while for $m\ge 3$ it is strictly stronger; it is the hypothesis on the local codes behind recent constructions of good quantum LDPC codes, good quantum locally testable codes, and quantum codes with transversal non-Clifford gates. No explicit family over a fixed field was previously known to achieve constant rate, linear distance for both the code and its dual, and 3-fold product expansion at growing length. We prove that for the one-point evaluation codes $C_i$ of length $N_i=728\cdot27^{\,i-1}$ and pole order $\lfloor N_i/5\rfloor$ on the Garcia--Stichtenoth tower over $\mathbb{F}_{729}$, the triple $(C_i,C_i,C_i)$ has product expansion with a constant independent of $i$. The dual codes $C_i^\perp$ then form an explicit fixed-field family of rate tending to $109/130$ and relative distance at least $8/65$. The proof is geometric: we view the words of the sum code as arrays on the product of three copies of the $i$-th curve of the tower, where the parity checks are sections of a line bundle. An exact generation theorem describes the sum-code words supported on the grid footprint of a suitable divisor. A support-localisation argument then shows that every low-weight array lies on such a divisor, after deleting a small number of coordinates. We also give a sufficient criterion for three-fold product expansion in terms of degree and genus ratios, yielding explicit families over every non-prime finite field of order at least $512$. The principal conclusions have been formally verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Cassie Ding, Min-Hsiu Hsieh

item.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the maximum number of common zeros in projective space of any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the cardinality of the finite field. This proves the conjecture of Beelen, Datta and Ghorpade and determines the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof uses Green's hyperplane restriction bound, combined with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. Wei duality then determines the hierarchy in sufficiently large degrees, recovering the complete hierarchy in every degree for the projective plane. Finally, we prove an upper bound valid in every degree, and conjecture that it is always sharp.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo San-Jos\'e

item.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.08356v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that K3 surfaces with no rational points over the finite field with $q$ elements exist if and only if $q \leq 11$. Our approach applies linear programming techniques to improve on generic sphere packing bounds for the discriminants of even rootless definite lattices. These bounds are applied to constrain the possible zeta functions of K3 surfaces with no rational points via the Artin--Tate formula. The remaining cases are ruled out by direct analysis of primitive embeddings of particular lattices into Niemeier lattices.
item.dc:creator: Asher Auel, Philip Engel, Kiran S. Kedlaya, Sair Shaikh

item.title: On supersoluble like groups of automorphisms of compact Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08391v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a not necessary full automorphism group of a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. We found sharp bounds for $|G|$ in the terms of $g$ when $G$ belongs to one of the following classes of finite groups sharing similar properties with supersoluble groups: 2-nilpotent, with the Sylow tower of supersoluble type, with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal cyclic primary subgroups, widely supersoluble, with submodular Sylow subgroups, with submodular cyclic primary subgroups and strongly supersoluble.
item.dc:creator: Viachaslau I. Murashka

item.title: Good minimal models with nowhere vanishing holomorphic $1$-forms
item.description: arXiv:2412.12582v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Popa and Schnell show that any holomorphic 1-form on a smooth projective variety of general type has zeros. In this article, we show that a smooth good minimal model has a holomorphic 1-form without zero if and only if it admits an analytic fiber bundle structure over a positive dimensional abelian variety.
item.dc:creator: Feng Hao, Zichang Wang, Lei Zhang

item.title: The automorphism groups of Kummer surfaces in characteristic two and their complex analogues
item.description: arXiv:2412.18902v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We calculate the automorphism group of the Kummer surface associated with a curve of genus 2 or the product of two elliptic curves in characteristic two under the assumption that the Kummer surface is a $K3$ surface. Moreover we discuss the complex $K3$ surfaces with the same Picard lattice as these Kummer surfaces. The paper has two appendices.
item.dc:creator: Shigeyuki Kondo, Shigeru Mukai

item.title: Algebraic Zhou valuations
item.description: arXiv:2505.19451v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we generalize Zhou valuations, originally defined on complex domains, to the framework of general schemes. We demonstrate that an algebraic version of the Jonsson--Musta\c{t}\u{a} conjecture is equivalent to the statement that every Zhou valuation is quasi-monomial. By introducing a mixed version of jumping numbers and Tian functions associated with valuations, we obtain characterizations of a valuation being a Zhou valuation or computing some jumping number using the Tian functions. Furthermore, we establish the correspondence between Zhou valuations in algebraic settings and their counterparts in analytic settings.
item.dc:creator: Shijie Bao, Qi'an Guan, Lin Zhou

item.title: Kobayashi hyperbolicity of complete linear systems on abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2512.10082v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a geometric condition ensuring that a very general element of a complete linear system on an abelian variety is Kobayashi hyperbolic. This can be seen as the counterpart of some classical results on very general hypersurfaces in projective spaces. Some related conjectures are also given, and involve a natural constant, the so-called basepoint-freeness threshold, associated with any polarized abelian variety $(A, L)$ detecting information about the hyperbolicity of $|L|$.
item.dc:creator: Federico Caucci

item.title: Anabelian perspectives in Galois-Teichm\"uller theory
item.description: arXiv:2603.02848v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By exploiting the arithmetic homotopy of the moduli spaces of curves, Galois-Teichm\"uller theory stands at the interface of braid-mapping class groups and of anabelian geometry. Starting from the classical braid-theoretic construction of the Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group, we review how anabelian geometry -- beginning with the foundational work of Nakamura -- provides the arithmetic mechanisms underlying its definition. We then explain how the combinatorial anabelian geometry developed by Hoshi and Mochizuki recasts these constructions within a purely group-theoretic and algorithmic framework. In particular, we describe how the group GT emerges as an anabelian object and how, once freed from an auxiliary or artificially imposed containers, the anabelian algorithms yield a combinatorial reconstruction of the absolute Galois group of rational numbers. The perspective developed here highlights a conceptual shift from explicit braid-theoretic computations to functorial and algorithmic forms of anabelian reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Collas

item.title: A theory of generalized Lam\'e curves
item.description: arXiv:2604.21880v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the generalized Lam'e equation (GLE) on an elliptic curve $E$ with multiple regular singularities $\mathbf{p} = (p_i)_{i = 1}^r$ of weights $\mathbf{n} = (n_i)_{i = 1}^r$. By analyzing the locus admitting quasi-periodic solutions, we construct two fundamental algebraic curves: (i) The generalized Lam'e curve (GLC), $\mathcal{Y}_{\mathbf{n}, \mathbf{p}}$, which lies in an affine bundle over $\operatorname{Sym}^n E$ for total weight $n:=\sum n_i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ and parametrizes generalized Hermite--Halphen ansatz solutions. (ii) The log-free curve, $V_{\mathbf{n}, \mathbf{p}}$, a non-complete intersection variety arising when all $n_i \in \frac{1}{2}\mathbb{N}$, which we prove is a reduced curve, confirming a conjecture of Wang. We analyze the GLC as an algebraic family over the pole configuration space. By studying the addition map$$\sigma \colon \operatorname{Sym}^n E \longrightarrow E,$$where we establish a generically finite, universal degree formula, we show that the geometry of boundary degenerations under pole collisions perfectly mirrors the tensor algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{C})$-modules within the BGG category $\mathcal{O}$. This provides the local structural limits needed to establish the global flatness of the GLC. Furthermore, we develop a framework of twisted isomonodromic deformations and construct $(\mathbf{n}, \mathbf{p})$-deformed pre-modular forms parameterized by twisted monodromy data $(t,s)$. Their vanishing solves the underlying monodromy problem and factorizes along boundary strata, allowing an arbitrary configuration to be continuously deformed down to the classical Lam'e equation. Finally, using an asymptotic scaling technique, we give a complete extension of Treibich's generic counting for $r=2$ symmetric pairs to all smooth elliptic curves.
item.dc:creator: You-Cheng Chou, Chin-Lung Wang, Po-Sheng Wu

item.title: The Quasisymmetric Grassmannian
item.description: arXiv:2604.24903v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a complex of toric varieties we call the quasisymmetric Grassmannian inside the Grassmannian of $r$-planes in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Each irreducible component is a positroid variety and an $S_n$ translate of a toric Richardson variety of ribbon shape. We describe it as the vanishing locus of equations $\Delta_A\Delta_{A'}=0$ in Pl\"ucker coordinates determined by a new noncrossing combinatorial object we call the quasisymmetric Johnson graph. We give an affine paving, and show that its cohomology ring is a quasisymmetric modification of the Borel presentation of the Grassmannian's cohomology, with fundamental quasisymmetric polynomials playing the role of Schur polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Nantel Bergeron, Lucas Gagnon, Hunter Spink, Vasu Tewari

item.title: Whittaker groups and hyperelliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2605.22406v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let K be a complete, non-archimedean valued field with a residue field of characteristic different from 2. A Whittaker group G is a discontinuous subgroup of PGL(2,K), freely generated by elements s_0,...,s_g of order two, each defined by a pair of fixed points {a_0,b_0},...,{a_g,b_g}. These fixed points are called ``in good position''. A subgroup W in G of index 2 is a Schottky group and produces a hyperelliptic Mumford curve Omega/W --> Omega/G = P^1, called `Whittaker curve', of genus g and with branch locus B in P^1(K). An explicit parametrization of Whittaker curves in terms of theta functions for W and G and the data of the fixed points, is developed. In particular, this allows one to express the branched points (and other data such as p-adic periods and p-adic heights) in terms of values of theta functions. A central theme of this paper is the relation between the fixed points and the branch locus. For a given configuration (P,m) of $g+1$ pairs of points in P^1, one defines a rigid space Fix_{P,m} of fixed points in good position with that configuration and a rigid space of branched points $ Branch_{P,m} in that configuration. A main result is that the natural morphism FB: Fix_{P,m} --> Branch_{P,m} is a rigid etale covering with Galois group {\pm 1}^{d-1} for some d>0. For all cases of genus g=2,3 (and for some more), an approximation of FB is computed which confirms the main result. Classification of Whittaker groups and analytic reductions of Whittaker curves is another important issue of this paper. The background material in this paper complements the work of L.~Gerritzen, G.~Van Steen, F.~Herrlich and others. It involves re-examination of some proofs, the derivation of properties of semi-stable analytic reductions and studying good position of fixed points.
item.dc:creator: Marius van der Put, Jaap Top

item.title: Non-Archimedean balanced metrics and their application to totally degenerate abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2606.15758v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a polarized complex manifold with discrete automorphism group, it is known that if the first Chern class admits a cscK metric, then the balanced metrics, which are characterized in terms of the algebro-geometric notion of Chow stability, approximate this cscK metric. In this paper, we study a non-Archimedean analogue of this phenomenon. In particular, we prove that such an analogue holds for polarized totally degenerate abelian varieties. As an application, we also show that, for a totally degenerating family of polarized abelian varieties, the validity of this non-Archimedean analogue yields a uniform estimate for the Calabi--Yau metrics on fibers sufficiently close to the degenerate fiber.
item.dc:creator: Keita Goto

item.title: Foliated and Mather-Jacobian discrepancies via tangential arcs
item.description: arXiv:2607.01809v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We express the log discrepancies of co-rank one foliations on normal varieties in terms of arc codimensions and differential orders. On smooth threefolds, if a foliation has simple singularities and its separatrices form an algebraic simple normal crossings divisor, we identify its foliated discrepancies with those of an ordinary pair for every divisor centred on the separatrices. This gives adjunction and log canonical threshold formulae. For algebraic images of the separatrices, we estimate changes in boundary orders caused by failure of ideal generation and by descent through the conductor. For locally complete intersection images, comparison on a common resolution yields criteria for equality of discrepancies and bounds on log canonical thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Maur\'icio Corr\^ea

item.title: Tautological classes on KSBA spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.19251v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the definitions of kappa, psi and lambda classes from the case of moduli spaces of stable curves to the higher-dimensional case of KSBA spaces, and prove a number of their basic properties.
item.dc:creator: Valery Alexeev

item.title: Counterexamples to the Jacobian conjecture in dimensions greater than two
item.description: arXiv:2608.00222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Jacobian conjecture, open since 1939, asks whether every polynomial map of $\C^n$ whose Jacobian determinant is a nonzero constant must have a polynomial inverse. It was refuted in dimension three by Alp\"oge on July 19, 2026, with an infinite family by Gallagher (July 20) and a geometric explanation by Speyer (July 23): the counterexample sweeps the tangent lines of a plane curve. We give a self-contained account of this tangent-sweep mechanism and generalize it from plane curves to direction fields on hypersurfaces. The resulting construction, including stabilization of the three-dimensional family, produces counterexamples in every dimension greater than two and, in each dimension, of arbitrarily large geometric degree (the number of preimages of a typical point). We work it out in five explicit maps: one three-dimensional of degree four, two four-dimensional of degrees five and ten, and two five-dimensional of degrees six and twelve. We show that our explicit examples in dimensions $n\ge4$ are not polynomially left-right equivalent to the counterexamples of Alp\"oge and Gallagher when these are embedded in $\C^n$ by adjoining identity coordinates. The counterexamples provide explicit examples of \'etale morphisms $\C^n\to\C^n$ that are not proper: they are everywhere unramified, and fail to be injective only through points escaping to infinity. All identities were verified in exact rational arithmetic. Part~\ref{part:equivalence} proves the higher-dimensional inequivalence results, and Appendix A determines exact fiber structures for the three-dimensional examples. A complete classification of the fibers of $F_4,F_5,F_6,F_7$ remains open.
item.dc:creator: Shuhong Gao

item.title: A counterexamples to the Polishchuk--Van den Bergh conjecture on curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.10147v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct an effective $S_3$ action on the smooth projective model of $y^2=t^{12h-5}+t$ for every $h\geq1$. Its quotient has genus $h$, and the fixed quotient for the three-cycle class consists of two points. We prove that the derived category of these two points admits no $\bbC$-linear exact fully faithful embedding into the equivariant derived category. This gives a counterexample to Conjecture A of Polishchuk and Van den Bergh. More generally, for a positive-genus quotient we compute the maximum number of completely orthogonal exceptional objects as $\Sm_i\lfloor e_i/2\rfloor$, where $e_i$ are the inertia orders. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for conjugacy-class decompositions with embeddings linear over the quotient, and construct kernels on the natural fibre products. For genus-zero quotients we obtain Euler-form bounds and exact capacities for all-two ramification with at least four branch points and for types $(2,3,3)$, $(2,3,4)$ and $(2,3,5)$.
item.dc:creator: Shengyong Pan

item.title: Characteristic cycles and Gevrey irregularity in hypergeometric families
item.description: arXiv:2610.12330v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the characteristic cycle multiplicities of $A$-hypergeometric systems are upper semicontinuous in the parameter for every rational projective weight, thereby proving a conjecture of Schulze and Walther [Duke Math. J. 142 (2008), 465--509]. The proof uses a specialization formula for filtered families satisfying a fixed product support condition, expressing the difference between the special and generic characteristic cycles as the characteristic cycle of the first Tor module. Combined with the Gevrey index theorem, this yields upper semicontinuity of generic Gevrey irregularity and of each of its graded dimensions. We also construct non-Cohen--Macaulay semigroup rings whose Gevrey dimensions are constant in the parameter despite the presence of a genuine irregular slope, showing that the Gevrey jump locus need not coincide with the full exceptional arrangement defined by Ext.
item.dc:creator: Sheng Tan

item.title: Quotients of Calabi-Yau Generalized Fermat manifolds and Log Enriques varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.21752v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties have attracted a lot of interest in the last years. In this paper we study Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties that are respectively \'etale and quasi-\'etale quotients of Calabi-Yau manifolds. We produce several examples by studying quotients of generalized Fermat manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. These are complete intersections of Fermat type manifolds all of the same degree and were described recently by Hidalgo, Hughes and Leyton-\'Alvarez. We describe all their quotients by a fixed-point-free automorphism. Most of the quotients are Log Enriques varieties or Calabi-Yau varieties with terminal singularities. In one case we get a family of Enriques manifolds which is a subfamily of a family described previously by Boissi\`ere, Camere and the third author, which is one of the two so far known families of Enriques manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. This family is obtained as an \'etale quotient of order two of a Calabi-Yau manifold complete intersection of quadrics, the other family is the Hilbert scheme of $n$ points on an Enriques surface. In the last part of the paper we show that these two families are different by computing their second Betti numbers, which are equal to one and eleven respectively.
item.dc:creator: Simone Billi, Ana Julisa Palomino, Alessandra Sarti

item.title: Effective Gromov-Witten computations for GKM spaces and a semisimple application
item.description: arXiv:2610.37273v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report a major update to our original software GKMtools and record multiple improvements in the computation of Gromov--Witten invariants of GKM spaces. This includes a refined divisor equation that reduces the complexity from exponential to linear in the number of marked points, three tricks to accelerate the computation of curve class relations in the GKM graph, and an implementation of Mihalcea's algorithm for homogeneous varieties using the equivariant quantum Chevalley formula. As an application, we prove that the small quantum cohomology of the type $E$ generalized Grassmannians $E_7/P_2,E_7/P_4,E_7/P_5,E_8/P_6$ is generically semisimple. These are precisely the remaining exceptional Grassmannians for which generic semisimplicity of small quantum cohomology was still unknown.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Holmes, Giosu\`e Muratore

item.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.03124v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We prove strict strong positivity for good prefixes with at most three repeated blocks after the first factor. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguy\^en's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential $m$-positive classes and on the solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li

item.title: PCF All The Way Down
item.description: arXiv:2611.06106v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down. A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Dupuy, Alon Levy, Thomas Tucker, Zhuoran Wang

item.title: Log canonical singularities of plurisubharmonic functions
item.description: arXiv:2312.16140v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A plurisubharmonic weight is \emph{log canonical} if it is at the critical point of turning non-integrable. Given a log canonical plurisubharmonic weight, we show that locally there always exists a log canonical `holomorphic' weight having the same non-integrable locus. The proof uses the theory of quasimonomial valuations developed by Jonsson-Musta\c{t}\u{a} and Xu, as well as the minimal model program over complex analytic spaces due to Fujino and Lyu-Murayama. As a consequence, we obtain that the non-integrable locus is seminormal.
item.dc:creator: Dano Kim, J\'anos Koll\'ar

item.title: Central simple algebras, Milnor $K$-theory and homogeneous spaces over complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2
item.description: arXiv:2501.01403v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field of dimension $2$. We prove the following statements on the arithmetic of $K$. - The ``period equals index'' property holds for central simple $K$-algebras. - If $K$ has characteristic $0$, for every prime $p$, every class in the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ is represented by a symbol. - Serre's Conjecture II holds for the field $K$. That is, for every semisimple and simply connected $K$-group $G$, the set $H^1(K,G)$ is trivial.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Gille, Diego Izquierdo, Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche

item.title: A simplified proof of the o-minimal Whitney Extension Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2603.14924v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a proof of the o-minimal version of the Whitney Extension Theorem simplified as compared to the original ones. A new simplifying ingredient is a definable variant of Urysohn's lemma for class $\mathcal{C}^q$ (see Section 3).
item.dc:creator: Beata Kocel-Cynk, Wies{\l}aw Paw{\l}ucki, Anna Valette

item.title: Semistable Reduction Theorem for Overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over Laurent Series Fields
item.description: arXiv:2604.17799v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the semistable reduction theorem for $\mathcal{E}^{\dag}_K$-valued and $K$-valued overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over $k((t))$-varieties which were introduced by Lazda and P\'{a}l. As an application, we prove the finite dimensionality of $\mathcal{E}^{\dag}_K$-valued rigid cohomology with compact support.
item.dc:creator: Yuanmin Liu

item.title: Minimal Filling Architectures for Polynomial Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2605.09609v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Minimal filling architectures describe the smallest hidden-layer widths for which the neurovariety of a polynomial neural network fills its ambient function space. It was conjectured that every such architecture has unimodal hidden widths. We construct counterexamples to this conjecture using a frontier search and certify the main example through finite-field Jacobian computations and recursive dimension bounds. In the opposite direction, we prove that every minimal filling architecture of depth at most three is unimodal. A nonunimodal minimal filling architecture of depth four shows that the depth bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Dao, Jose Israel Rodriguez

item.title: On the First Caustic of Elliptical Billiards
item.description: arXiv:2606.04132v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A point source of light is placed inside a billiard with a smooth, convex, closed boundary. For any integer $n$, the $n$-th caustic by reflection, denoted by $\Gamma_n$, is the envelope of light rays that have undergone $n$ reflections in such a billiard after emanating from the source. It has been conjectured by Gil Bor and Serge Tabachnikov that for an elliptical billiard, $\Gamma_n$ has exactly four ordinary cusps; this problem is a billiard variation of Jacobi's Last Geometric Statement, which concerns the number of cusps in the conjugate locus of a point on an ellipsoid. Gil Bor, Mark Spivakovsky, and Serge Tabachnikov have proven that $\Gamma_n$ has at least four ordinary cusps. In this paper, we present a proof that $\Gamma_1$ has exactly four ordinary cusps, using billiards in complex spaces.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandra Uskova

item.title: Finite-coefficient K-theory of henselian valued fields and Gersten injectivity
item.description: arXiv:2608.18789v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $W$ be a henselian valuation ring with fraction field $L$, residue field $k$, and value group $\Gamma_W$. Let $N=\ell^\nu$ be invertible in $W$. Choose an ordered $\mathbf Z/N$-basis $B$ of $\Gamma_W/N\Gamma_W$. Products of suitable classes define an equivalence of complete filtered spectra $$ \bigoplus_{\substack{J\subseteq B\\J\text{ finite}}} \Sigma^{|J|}\operatorname{Fil}_{\mathrm{mot}}^{\bullet-|J|} K(k;\mathbf Z/N) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Fil}_{\mathrm{mot}}^{\bullet} K(L;\mathbf Z/N) $$ The summand indexed by $\varnothing$ is the generic restriction map, after the rigidity equivalence $K(W;\mathbf Z/N)\simeq K(k;\mathbf Z/N)$, and is therefore split injective. Independently of this splitting, excision yields a lifting theorem for regular henselian pairs. In particular, this yields finite-coefficient Gersten injectivity for noetherian henselian regular local rings. Applications to completions along regular primes give relative and sometimes nonhenselian examples. More generally, if $P$ is a Pr\"ufer ring and $R$ is a henselian local ind-smooth $P$-algebra, then $R$ is a domain and $K_n(R;\mathbf Z/N)\to K_n(\operatorname{Frac}(R);\mathbf Z/N)$ is injective for every $n$, provided $N\in R^\times$. These injectivity consequences extend from prime-power to arbitrary finite invertible coefficients by primary decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Niels Feld

item.title: Profinite Non-Rigidity of Arithmetic Lattices and the K\"ahler Property
item.description: arXiv:2609.31523v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the profinite non-rigidity of arithmetic lattices and its implications for the K\"ahler property. In the first part, we characterize the absolute Dynkin types that admit non-isomorphic real forms of higher-rank Lie groups containing torsion-free arithmetic lattices with isomorphic profinite completions. In the second part, as a geometric application, we answer a question asked independently by Arapura and Libgober, by showing that the K\"ahlerness of finitely presented, residually finite groups is not determined by its profinite completion.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Du, Feng Hao, Kejia Zhu

item.title: Log-concavity and unimodality of cluster monomials in fan coordinates of type A_n
item.description: arXiv:2610.09312v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every cluster monomial of type A_n is log-concave and unimodal with respect to its Laurent expansion in a fan initial cluster. We derive a coefficient formula for laminar interval products arising from compatible diagonals in the polygon model. This gives partial affirmative answers to the log-concavity conjecture of Chen-Huang-Sun and the unimodality conjecture of Chen. Our result for cluster A-varieties also complements Shen's study on the supports of products of canonical basis elements for cluster X-varieties of type A_n.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Chen

item.title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
item.description: arXiv:2610.30395v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.
item.dc:creator: Ruben Louis

item.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.40639v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that all compact hyperk\"ahler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojevi\'c and Stelzig, proving that in the context of pluripotential homotopy theory they play the same role as compact K\"ahler manifolds in rational homotopy theory. Indeed, the main result arises from general algebraic considerations on categories of objects with more differentials, that of $n$-complexes and commutative $n$-differential graded algebras. For them we discuss a standard model category structure, introduce a generalization of the $\partial\bar{\partial}$-Lemma and establish an algebraic formality theorem.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Pio Contr\`o
